description: Width tiers for Dance — Years 3-4 band
subject: Dance

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single task context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term. For Y3-4 Dance, minimum is typically one choreographic or performance context with basic element/skill application.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope from the elaboration range — covers the breadth of contexts, stimuli, and skills a well-taught Y3-4 student would engage with across the band.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions adding new task contexts, cultural communities, collaborative configurations or extended inquiry. First Nations elaborations appear in wider.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. Y3-4 elaborations are dance-strand specific with First Nations content foregrounded in E02.

AC9ADA4C01.minimum_width: Choreograph a dance with a clear beginning, middle and end communicating one idea — using at least two element choices; working with a partner to combine and extend.
AC9ADA4C01.typical_width: Choreograph dances communicating ideas, perspectives and/or meaning across multiple stimuli: improvising and combining locomotor/non-locomotor movements; using Viewpoints to plan and refine structure; incorporating contrast and repetition; creating dance communicating connection to Country/Place following appropriate ICIP protocols.
wider: Use learning from dances that communicate First Nations Australians' connection to Country/Place to frame and develop own choreographic intent — creating a dance communicating students' connection to a specific place in their community
Investigate how a dance from a cultural celebration communicates specific ideas — using this research to enrich and contextualise own choreographic intent
Layer a second structural device (e.g. canon, contrast section, call-and-response) into an existing dance — deepening the communication of meaning through structural complexity
elaborations: improvising using movements from a dance they have learnt and using elements to develop sequences based on original movements
using Viewpoints to frame questions about choreography being developed
creating dance sequences by combining fundamental locomotor and non-locomotor movements at various levels and directions
using learning from First Nations Australians' connection to Country/Place to devise dance communicating their own connection

AC9ADA4D01.minimum_width: Demonstrate habitual safe practice (warm-up, surface awareness); refine technical quality in at least two movement types in response to feedback.
AC9ADA4D01.typical_width: Develop habitual safe dance practice including warm-up and cool-down; explore known movements to find alternative ways of performing them; use contrast and repetition to generate new movement; develop body awareness and refine technical skills (control, accuracy, alignment, strength, balance, coordination) in response to feedback; use elements to communicate ideas through cultural stories and character movement.
wider: Lead a warm-up sequence for a small group — making decisions about what to include and why, developing understanding of safe practice as a design activity
Focus sustained technical practice on one complex movement type — setting specific quality targets and tracking improvement across sessions
Explore how cultural stories can be shared through dance — using element choices to represent character walks, emotions, and mood of specific narrative settings
elaborations: exploring known movements to find alternative ways of performing them at different levels, directions, sizes, body parts
using contrast and repetition to explore and generate new movement in response to stimuli
exploring how elements of dance can be used to communicate ideas from cultural stories
developing the habit of always using safe dance practice including warm-up and cool-down
developing body awareness and refining technical skills in response to teacher feedback

AC9ADA4E01.minimum_width: Identify two different purposes for dance from two different cultural or temporal contexts; compare at least one similarity and one difference between them.
AC9ADA4E01.typical_width: Explore where, why and how dance is choreographed and performed across cultures, times and places: celebration, narrative, entertainment; learning dances from a range of cultures including countries in Asia; using Viewpoints to compare dances; exploring 'dance crazes' and widely shared dances across cultures.
wider: Investigate a dance craze or widely known dance — tracing its origin, geographic spread, and cultural transformation across different contexts
Explore dances from a country or region in Asia — identifying cultural purpose, performance occasions, and what is communicated
Investigate how a specific dance tradition has changed over time while retaining core purpose — exploring what persistence through change reveals about cultural values
elaborations: identifying meaning and describing purposes that dance is created for across a range of cultures
learning dances created for different purposes such as entertainment, dance crazes
using Viewpoints to ask questions about similarities, where dances are performed

AC9ADA4E02.minimum_width: Describe one way a First Nations Australian dance communicates connection to or responsibility for Country/Place; identify at least one element of dance that carries this meaning.
AC9ADA4E02.typical_width: Explore how First Nations Australians use dance to express connection to and responsibility for Country/Place: communicating knowledge about seasons, wind, water, fire, sustainable practices; observing element use in dances about Country/Place with community representatives or co-created resources; collecting and sharing information about dances performed at festivals or ceremonies.
wider: Explore screen-based storytelling used by First Nations Australians to maintain cultural ways of life — comparing with dance forms used for similar purposes of cultural maintenance

Compare element use across two First Nations Australian dances from different communities — identifying how different environmental or seasonal knowledge is communicated through different element choices
Explore cultural accounts of specific places through dance with community representation — noting how particular movements carry particular place-knowledge
elaborations: collecting and sharing information about dances for festivals or ceremonies; reflecting on how they communicate knowledge about Country/Place
exploring how First Nations Australians use dance to express connection to and responsibility for Country/Place including seasonal knowledge
exploring screen-based storytelling to maintain unique ways of life
observing how elements are used in dances communicating connection to Country/Place
exploring movements in dances with community representatives or co-created resources

AC9ADA4P01.minimum_width: Perform one dance to the class using at least one expressive skill (projection or focus); share meaning and intended purpose; provide one constructive feedback comment to a peer.
AC9ADA4P01.typical_width: Practise and perform dances in informal class settings; use expressive skills (projection, focus) to communicate ideas; present via screen-based technologies or online platforms; be an attentive audience member; share meaning and purpose through words, images, learnt terminology, movement or drawing; participate in class debrief discussions.
wider: Present a dance on a digital school platform (e.g. LMS) — adapting the introduction for a remote or asynchronous audience context
View a recording of own performance — comparing self-perception with observed performance, setting one specific development goal
Receive and act on peer feedback — documenting the change made and its effect on the performance
elaborations: using expressive skills such as projection and focus to communicate to an audience
presenting dance using screen-based technologies or online platforms
being an attentive audience member during class performances and providing constructive feedback
sharing meaning and intended purposes using own words, images, learnt terminology, movement or drawing
